# Purpose

This problem develops load-path reasoning, torque equilibrium, internal resultants, torsional shear stress, section-property selection, and engineering judgment. Award credit for a consistent torque sign convention, correct cumulative internal torques, a labeled torque diagram, proper circular-shaft stress equations, whole-millimeter upward wall-thickness selection, verification, and a bounded engineering recommendation.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The base model assumes circular prismatic shaft segments, concentrated static torques, ideal bearings that do not resist shaft-axis torque, linear elasticity, and Saint-Venant torsion. A complete design also requires gear-force bending, combined stress, fatigue, keyways and shoulders, stress concentrations, angular twist, critical speed, bearing selection, tolerances, and applicable standards.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation: 15%;
- idealization: 15%;
- internal resultants: 20%;
- stress analysis: 15%;
- sizing and verification: 25%;
- engineering recommendation and limitations: 10%.
